newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rules out Mobutu-Kabila meeting.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rules out Mobutu-Kabila meeting.

text.p: Zaire's government once again ruled out direct peace talks between President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, dismissing Kabila as a puppet of neighbouring Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi.
"Kabila is a mere puppet. How can President Mobutu negotiate with him while it's known that he is only a front man for the aggressors," Deputy Foreign Minister Lokondo Yoka told reporters.

"Zaire has been attacked by Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda," he said. "If any Zairean who opposes the regime can take up arms to seize power with the support of foreign countries, this would be unfortunate."
South Africa's Nelson Mandela tried to organise negotiations between the two men.
Kabila, a veteran Mobutu foe, has called for him to go but has also called for face-to-face talks.
Mobutu, who had cancer surgery in Europe in August, is at his villa in France. It is not clear when he plans to return.
Lokondo said the army, which has based its operations in the war zone in Zaire's third city Kisangani, was reorganising.
The rebels, who took up arms in October and seized towns and territory in the east, have named Kisangani as the next target.
